items.text: Full code review of the topology pipeline found NO proto mapping mismatches. All 7 node types (backlog, initiative, capture, scenario, execution, agent-activity, agent-run) are consistently handled in Go encoding (proto_response.go), TS decoding (graph-service.ts:mapProtoNode), NODE_TYPE_MAP, and ENTITY_REGISTRY. H3 (proto parsing failure) is now LOW probability. The default case in mapProtoNode() logs a warning and creates a fallback node rather than silently dropping — so if proto was the issue, we'd see console warnings.

Found a minor bug in projection_topology.go:137 — capture classification edges use `backlogItemKey(ci.Kind, ci.Title)` where `ci.Title` is likely the human-readable title, not the slug-style name used in backlog item keys. This means `classified_as` edges from captures to backlog items likely never match `itemIndex`. This is a real bug but wouldn't cause a blank view — it only affects capture-to-backlog edges.

items.topic: What does the API return when you curl the topology endpoint?
items.context: Per the round 1 decision (API-first diagnostics), the critical first step is checking whether the backend returns nodes. Run: `curl -s localhost:<port>/api/v1/graph?lens=topology | jq '.meta'` (or pipe through `jq length` on `.nodes`). This single check bisects the problem between backend and frontend.

options.label: API returns nodes (nodeCount > 0)
options.rationale: The backend is working correctly. The issue is frontend — filtering, clustering, or rendering. Next step: inspect browser console and graph store state.

options.label: API returns 0 nodes
options.rationale: The issue is backend filtering. Despite active items in `swarm-manager backlog list`, the topology projection's completed/archived filter may be too aggressive, or LoadAll() returns an error silently.

options.label: API returns an error (non-200 status)
options.rationale: The endpoint itself is failing — could be a missing dependency, database error, or handler crash. Check API logs.

options.label: Can't test right now / swarm-manager isn't running
options.rationale: We'll need to start swarm-manager first, or adjust the diagnostic approach to be code-analysis only.

items.topic: Have you checked the browser console when loading the topology view?
items.context: The frontend has console logging at key points: mapProtoNode() logs warnings for unknown node data cases, and fetchGraph() likely surfaces errors. Checking the console would reveal proto mapping failures (H3), JavaScript errors, or network failures. Also check localStorage key 'swarm-manager.graph.settings.v6' for filter state.

options.label: Console shows errors or warnings — will paste details
options.rationale: Specific errors would immediately pinpoint the broken layer. Proto warnings = H3, fetch errors = H6, React errors = rendering bug.

options.label: Console is clean — no errors or warnings
options.rationale: Rules out proto mapping failures and JavaScript errors. Issue is likely filter state (H2) or clustering (H4). Next step: check localStorage filters and try toggling grouping mode.

options.label: Haven't checked yet / will check and report back
options.rationale: This is a quick check that provides high diagnostic value.

items.topic: Where should pipeline-stage diagnostic logging go?
items.context: Per round 1 decision d3:B (fix + defensive improvement), we want to add diagnostic logging so blank-view issues surface faster. The question is the right granularity — too little misses issues, too much creates noise.

options.label: Log at 3 stages: fetchGraph response, post-filter, post-layout
options.rationale: Covers the major pipeline boundaries. fetchGraph logs API response node/edge count; filterGraphNodes logs how many nodes survived filtering; layoutedNodes logs post-layout count. Three log lines per graph load. Recommended because it covers the most likely failure points without noise.

options.label: Only log when nodeCount drops to 0 at any stage
options.rationale: Zero-noise approach — only fires when something goes wrong. But misses partial data loss (e.g., 50 nodes filtered to 2).

options.label: Full pipeline trace (every stage including clustering, edge filtering, styling)
options.rationale: Maximum observability, but generates 6+ log lines per graph load. Useful for development but noisy in production.
